i18n.en: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

notes.official: *wayəḏabbēr YHWH ʾel-mōšeh lēʾmōr* 'And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying'. Leviticus 17 opens the block of laws that scholarship calls the Holiness Code (Lev 17-26), and its first law concerns slaughter and blood. Names follow the Torah volumes (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-torah`): 'Moses', as exodus-woh prints it.

paragraphs.text: דַּבֵּ֨ר אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֜ן וְאֶל־בָּנָ֗יו וְאֶל֙ כָּל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: "Speak to Aharon and to his sons and to all the children of Yisra'el, and say to them, 'This is the thing which YHWH has commanded, saying:

notes.official: 'Aharon' = Aaron; 'Yisra'el' = Israel (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-torah`). YHWH's speech to Moses is in double quotation marks, and the words Moses is to say to the priests and the people ('This is the thing which YHWH has commanded ...') are in single marks (`direct-speech-quotation-marks-convention-torah`); the law of vv 3-7 follows the colon. *zeh haddāḇār* 'This is the thing': the formula that introduces a divine command (Ex 16:16; 35:4).

paragraphs.text: אִ֥ישׁ אִישׁ֙ מִבֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׁחַ֜ט שׁ֥וֹר אוֹ־כֶ֛שֶׂב אוֹ־עֵ֖ז בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה א֚וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִשְׁחַ֔ט מִח֖וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

i18n.en: Any man of the house of Yisra'el who slaughters an ox or a lamb or a goat in the camp, or who slaughters it outside the camp,

notes.official: *ʾîš ʾîš* 'any man' is the distributive of legal texts (ASV 'What man soever'). *šāḥaṭ* is the ordinary verb for slaughtering an animal, for food or for sacrifice. Vv 3-4 require that every ox, lamb or goat slaughtered in or outside the camp be brought to the tent of meeting. Whether the law forbids all slaughter away from the sanctuary (Milgrom, *Leviticus 17-22*, AB 3A, 2000) or only sacrifice there is debated. Deut 12:15-25 later permits profane slaughter away from the one sanctuary.

paragraphs.text: וְאֶל־פֶּ֜תַח אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵד֮ לֹ֣א הֱבִיאוֹ֒ לְהַקְרִ֤יב קָרְבָּן֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה לִפְנֵ֖י מִשְׁכַּ֣ן יְהוָ֑ה דָּ֣ם יֵחָשֵׁ֞ב לָאִ֤ישׁ הַהוּא֙ דָּ֣ם שָׁפָ֔ךְ וְנִכְרַ֛ת הָאִ֥ישׁ הַה֖וּא מִקֶּ֥רֶב עַמּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: and has not brought it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to present it as an offering to YHWH before the tabernacle of YHWH, blood shall be reckoned to that man; he has shed blood, and that man shall be cut off from among his people;

notes.official: *dām yēḥāšēḇ lāʾîš hahûʾ dām šāp̄āḵ* 'blood shall be reckoned to that man; he has shed blood': slaughter outside the sanctuary is counted as bloodshed, the expression used for homicide (Gen 9:6; Num 35:33). *ləhaqrîḇ qorbān* 'to present it as an offering' (central `qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`). *wəniḵraṯ hāʾîš hahûʾ miqqereḇ ʿammô* 'and that man shall be cut off from among his people' is the karet penalty (central `karet-penalty-cut-off-from-people`), here with *hāʾîš* 'the man' as its subject, so the line prints 'that man'.

paragraphs.text: לְמַעַן֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָבִ֜יאוּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֶֽת־זִבְחֵיהֶם֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֵ֣ם זֹבְחִים֮ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הַשָּׂדֶה֒ וֶֽהֱבִיאֻ֣ם לַֽיהוָ֗ה אֶל־פֶּ֛תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵ֖ד אֶל־הַכֹּהֵ֑ן וְזָ֨בְח֜וּ זִבְחֵ֧י שְׁלָמִ֛ים לַֽיהוָ֖ה אוֹתָֽם׃

i18n.en: so that the children of Yisra'el may bring their sacrifices, which they are sacrificing in the open field, that they may bring them to YHWH, to the entrance of the tent of meeting, to the priest, and sacrifice them as sacrifices of peace-offerings to YHWH.

notes.official: *ʿal-pənê haśśāḏeh* 'in the open field': the verse states the law's purpose, that sacrifices hitherto offered in the countryside be brought to the priest at the tent. *zibḥê šəlāmîm* 'sacrifices of peace-offerings' (ASV; NRSV 'sacrifices of well-being'), under central `qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: וְזָרַ֨ק הַכֹּהֵ֤ן אֶת־הַדָּם֙ עַל־מִזְבַּ֣ח יְהוָ֔ה פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וְהִקְטִ֣יר הַחֵ֔לֶב לְרֵ֥יחַ נִיחֹ֖חַ לַיהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: And the priest shall dash the blood on the altar of YHWH at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and burn the fat for a soothing aroma to YHWH.

notes.official: *wəzāraq ... ʾeṯ-haddām* 'dash the blood' (ASV 'sprinkle'), and *rêaḥ nîḥōaḥ* 'a soothing aroma' (ASV 'a sweet savor'), under central `qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus` and `reach-hannichoach`.

paragraphs.text: וְלֹא־יִזְבְּח֥וּ עוֹד֙ אֶת־זִבְחֵיהֶ֔ם לַשְּׂעִירִ֕ם אֲשֶׁ֛ר הֵ֥ם זֹנִ֖ים אַחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם חֻקַּ֥ת עוֹלָ֛ם תִּֽהְיֶה־זֹּ֥את לָהֶ֖ם לְדֹרֹתָֽם׃

i18n.en: And they shall no longer sacrifice their sacrifices to the goat-demons, after whom they prostitute themselves. This shall be a statute forever to them throughout their generations.'

notes.official: *laśśəʿîrim ʾăšer hēm zōnîm ʾaḥărêhem* 'to the goat-demons, after whom they prostitute themselves' (overlay `seirim-goat-demons-leviticus-17-7`). *śāʿîr* is the ordinary word for a he-goat (Lev 16:5-26), and the ASV prints 'the he-goats'. Here the *śəʿîrîm* receive sacrifices and are the object of cultic infidelity, so they are beings that can be worshipped. The same plural names creatures of the ruins in Isa 13:21; 34:14 and cult figures in 2 Chr 11:15 (HALOT *śāʿîr* II; NRSV, NJPS 'goat-demons'). The verb *zānâ* is used figuratively for cultic infidelity (Ex 34:15-16; Lev 20:5-6) and takes the modern register of central `zonah-prostitute-status-vocabulary-cross-corpus` (ASV 'play the harlot'). *ḥuqqaṯ ʿôlām* 'a statute forever'. YHWH's commanded words, opened at v 2, close here.

paragraphs.text: וַאֲלֵהֶ֣ם תֹּאמַ֔ר אִ֥ישׁ אִישׁ֙ מִבֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּמִן־הַגֵּ֖ר אֲשֶׁר־יָג֣וּר בְּתוֹכָ֑ם אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲלֶ֥ה עֹלָ֖ה אוֹ־זָֽבַח׃

i18n.en: And you shall say to them, 'Any man of the house of Yisra'el, or of the sojourners who sojourn among them, who offers a burnt-offering or a sacrifice,

notes.official: *ûmin-haggēr ʾăšer-yāḡûr bəṯôḵām* 'or of the sojourners who sojourn among them': *gēr* takes the English of its verb *gûr* 'sojourn' (central `megurim-patriarchal-sojourner-self-identity-gur-root`; overlay `ger-toshav-sojourner-resident-leviticus-25`). The ASV has 'the strangers'. From here on, each law of the chapter binds the *gēr* as well as the Israelite. *ʿōlâ ʾô-zāḇaḥ* 'a burnt-offering or a sacrifice' (central `olah-burnt-offering`).

paragraphs.text: וְאֶל־פֶּ֜תַח אֹ֤הֶל מוֹעֵד֙ לֹ֣א יְבִיאֶ֔נּוּ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת אֹת֖וֹ לַיהוָ֑ה וְנִכְרַ֛ת הָאִ֥ישׁ הַה֖וּא מֵעַמָּֽיו׃

i18n.en: and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to offer it to YHWH, that man shall be cut off from his people.

notes.official: The karet formula again, with *hāʾîš* 'that man' as subject and *mēʿammāyw* 'from his people', literally 'from his kin' (central `karet-penalty-cut-off-from-people`).

paragraphs.text: וְאִ֨ישׁ אִ֜ישׁ מִבֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וּמִן־הַגֵּר֙ הַגָּ֣ר בְּתוֹכָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֹאכַ֖ל כָּל־דָּ֑ם וְנָתַתִּ֣י פָנַ֗י בַּנֶּ֙פֶשׁ֙ הָאֹכֶ֣לֶת אֶת־הַדָּ֔ם וְהִכְרַתִּ֥י אֹתָ֖הּ מִקֶּ֥רֶב עַמָּֽהּ׃

i18n.en: And any man of the house of Yisra'el, or of the sojourners who sojourn among them, who eats any blood, I will set my face against the nefesh that eats the blood, and will cut that nefesh off from among its people.

notes.official:
*wənāṯattî p̄ānay bannep̄eš hāʾōḵeleṯ ʾeṯ-haddām wəhiḵrattî ʾōṯāh miqqereḇ ʿammāh* 'I will set my face against the nefesh that eats the blood, and will cut that nefesh off from among its people'. This is the first-person form of the karet formula, and its subject is *nep̄eš*, which the central `karet-penalty-cut-off-from-people` entry prints as 'nefesh' (ASV 'soul'; NRSV 'that person'). The feminine pronouns *ʾōṯāh* and *ʿammāh* agree with *nep̄eš*.

Vv 10-15 use *nep̄eš* six times, and English needs three words for them (overlay `nefesh-blood-life-leviticus-17`): 'nefesh' here, under the karet formula; 'life' in the blood-life equation of vv 11 and 14 (central basar-b-nafsho-damo, as Gen 9:4); 'lives' in v 11b; and 'person' for the distributive 'every *nep̄eš*' of vv 12 and 15 (nefesh-scope-torah). The word is the same throughout, and the argument depends on it: the *nep̄eš* that eats blood forfeits itself, because the *nep̄eš* of the flesh is in the blood.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י נֶ֣פֶשׁ הַבָּשָׂר֮ בַּדָּ֣ם הִוא֒ וַאֲנִ֞י נְתַתִּ֤יו לָכֶם֙ עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ לְכַפֵּ֖ר עַל־נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶ֑ם כִּֽי־הַדָּ֥ם ה֖וּא בַּנֶּ֥פֶשׁ יְכַפֵּֽר׃

i18n.en: For the life of the flesh is in the blood; and I have given it to you upon the altar to make atonement for your lives; for it is the blood that makes atonement by reason of the life.

notes.official:
*kî nep̄eš habbāśār baddām hîʾ* 'For the life of the flesh is in the blood': the equation of Gen 9:4, with the same rendering (central `basar-b-nafsho-damo`; overlay `nefesh-blood-life-leviticus-17`; ASV and NJPS 'life'). *wāʾănî nəṯattîw lāḵem ʿal-hammizbēaḥ ləḵappēr ʿal-nap̄šōṯêḵem* 'and I have given it to you upon the altar to make atonement for your lives': the ASV has 'for your souls', and NJPS 'for your lives'.

*kî-haddām hûʾ bannep̄eš yəḵappēr* 'for it is the blood that makes atonement by reason of the life'. The preposition *bə-* is read in three ways. The ASV takes it as instrumental, 'by reason of the life'. NJPS takes it as *bet essentiae*, 'it is the blood, as life, that effects expiation'. Others take it as *bet pretii*, 'in exchange for the life', a ransom of life for life (B. J. Schwartz, 'The Prohibitions Concerning the "Eating" of Blood in Leviticus 17', 1991). Milgrom (*Leviticus 17-22*, AB 3A, 2000) reads *kippēr* here as 'ransom'. The line keeps the ASV.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *Let's Welcome the Extra-Terrestrials* (ch. 1) quotes this verse as 'For the soul of the flesh is in the blood', beside Gen 9:4-5, to argue that every living being, not only humans, has a 'soul', that this soul is its blood, which the book identifies with the genetic code, and that there is no ethereal soul that leaves the body at death. The canon's 'soul' and the line's 'life' render the same word *nep̄eš*. The line follows the corpus rendering of the blood-life equation and does not encode the genetic-code reading.

paragraphs.text: עַל־כֵּ֤ן אָמַ֙רְתִּי֙ לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כָּל־נֶ֥פֶשׁ מִכֶּ֖ם לֹא־תֹ֣אכַל דָּ֑ם וְהַגֵּ֛ר הַגָּ֥ר בְּתוֹכְכֶ֖ם לֹא־יֹ֥אכַל דָּֽם׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Therefore I said to the children of Yisra'el, "No person among you shall eat blood, nor shall the sojourner who sojourns among you eat blood."

notes.official: *kol-nep̄eš mikkem lōʾ-ṯōʾḵal dām* 'No person among you shall eat blood': the distributive *kol-nep̄eš* is 'person' under `nefesh-scope-torah` (ASV 'No soul of you'). YHWH quotes his own earlier command to Israel, which is a third level of speech inside the words Moses is to say, which are themselves inside YHWH's speech, so it takes double marks inside the single marks (`direct-speech-quotation-marks-convention-torah`).

paragraphs.text: וְאִ֨ישׁ אִ֜ישׁ מִבְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וּמִן־הַגֵּר֙ הַגָּ֣ר בְּתוֹכָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָצ֜וּד צֵ֥יד חַיָּ֛ה אוֹ־ע֖וֹף אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵאָכֵ֑ל וְשָׁפַךְ֙ אֶת־דָּמ֔וֹ וְכִסָּ֖הוּ בֶּעָפָֽר׃

i18n.en: And any man of the children of Yisra'el, or of the sojourners who sojourn among them, who hunts game, a beast or a bird that may be eaten, shall pour out its blood and cover it with dust.

notes.official: *ʾăšer yāṣûḏ ṣêḏ ḥayyâ ʾô-ʿôp̄* 'who hunts game, a beast or a bird': game cannot be brought to the altar, so its blood is poured out and covered with dust (*ʿāp̄ār*). Exposed blood cries out (Gen 4:10; Ezek 24:7-8).

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־נֶ֣פֶשׁ כָּל־בָּשָׂ֗ר דָּמ֣וֹ בְנַפְשׁוֹ֮ הוּא֒ וָֽאֹמַר֙ לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל דַּ֥ם כָּל־בָּשָׂ֖ר לֹ֣א תֹאכֵ֑לוּ כִּ֣י נֶ֤פֶשׁ כָּל־בָּשָׂר֙ דָּמ֣וֹ הִ֔וא כָּל־אֹכְלָ֖יו יִכָּרֵֽת׃

i18n.en: For as for the life of all flesh, its blood is with its life; therefore I said to the children of Yisra'el, "You shall not eat the blood of any flesh, for the life of all flesh is its blood; whoever eats it shall be cut off."

notes.official: *kî-nep̄eš kol-bāśār dāmô ḇənap̄šô hûʾ* 'For as for the life of all flesh, its blood is with its life'. The clause is compressed: literally 'the life of all flesh, its blood, in its life it is'. The ASV supplies '[all one]' ('the blood thereof is all one with the life thereof'), and NJPS reads 'its blood is its life'. The LXX lacks *bənap̄šô*, which gives the simpler sense that NJPS also expresses. The line keeps the MT preposition without supplement, which echoes the *bənap̄šô* of Gen 9:4 ('flesh with its life, its blood', central `basar-b-nafsho-damo`), and records the shorter text under `mt-baseline-ketiv-qere-and-accent-division-torah`. The second half states the equation outright: *kî nep̄eš kol-bāśār dāmô hîʾ* 'for the life of all flesh is its blood'. *kol-ʾōḵəlāyw yikkārēṯ* 'whoever eats it shall be cut off' (central `karet-penalty-cut-off-from-people`). On *nep̄eš* in vv 10-15 see the note at v 10.

paragraphs.text: וְכָל־נֶ֗פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תֹּאכַ֤ל נְבֵלָה֙ וּטְרֵפָ֔ה בָּאֶזְרָ֖ח וּבַגֵּ֑ר וְכִבֶּ֨ס בְּגָדָ֜יו וְרָחַ֥ץ בַּמַּ֛יִם וְטָמֵ֥א עַד־הָעֶ֖רֶב וְטָהֵֽר׃

i18n.en: And every person who eats what dies of itself or what is torn by beasts, whether native or sojourner, shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and be unclean until the evening; then he shall be clean.

notes.official: *wəḵol-nep̄eš ʾăšer tōʾḵal nəḇēlâ ûṭərēp̄â* 'And every person who eats what dies of itself or what is torn by beasts': 'person' for the distributive *kol-nep̄eš* (`nefesh-scope-torah`; ASV 'every soul'). *bāʾezrāḥ ûḇaggēr* 'whether native or sojourner'. The carcass makes the eater unclean until evening, and washing restores him. Deut 14:21 forbids the Israelite to eat *nəḇēlâ* at all and allows it to be given to the *gēr*, which is one of the known differences between the Holiness Code and Deuteronomy (Milgrom, AB 3A).

paragraphs.text: וְאִם֙ לֹ֣א יְכַבֵּ֔ס וּבְשָׂר֖וֹ לֹ֣א יִרְחָ֑ץ וְנָשָׂ֖א עֲוֺנֽוֹ׃ (פ)

i18n.en: But if he does not wash them, nor bathe his flesh, then he shall bear his iniquity.'"

notes.official: *wənāśāʾ ʿăwōnô* 'then he shall bear his iniquity' (central `avon-iniquity-cross-corpus-keyword`): the man who fails to wash bears the consequence of his impurity himself. The words Moses is to say (opened at v 8) and YHWH's speech to Moses (opened at v 2) close here.
